title: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
paragraphs: BBC Radio 4 adaptation of Tolkien’s novel. Frozen GRH set is the thirteen-part hour-long edit derived from the original 26 half-hour 1981 serial, not the original 26-part broadcast sequence.

GRH documents the program through Original 26-part BBC Radio 4 serial (March 8, 1981 to August 30, 1981) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]] and BBC 13-part hour edit (July 17, 1982 to October 9, 1982) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Brian Sibley (radio adaptor on 13 recordings), Gerard Murphy (narrator on 13 recordings), Ian Holm (performer on 13 recordings), Jane Morgan (director on 13 recordings), Michael Bakewell (radio adaptor on 13 recordings), Penny Leicester (director on 13 recordings), and Stephen Oliver (composer on 13 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include epic fantasy, quest and fellowship, the One Ring and burden of power, Middle-earth, war against Sauron, and BBC prestige literary adaptation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Original 26-part BBC Radio 4 serial, Thirteen-part hour-long re-edit, Earlier BBC Lord of the Rings adaptation, and 2002 BBC reissue and rerun.

BBC Radio 4 adaptation of Tolkien’s novel. Frozen GRH set is the thirteen-part hour-long edit derived from the original 26 half-hour 1981 serial, not the original 26-part broadcast sequence.

GRH documents the program through Original 26-part BBC Radio 4 serial (March 8, 1981 to August 30, 1981) on BBC Radio 4 and BBC 13-part hour edit (July 17, 1982 to October 9, 1982) on BBC Radio 4.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Brian Sibley (radio adaptor on 13 recordings), Gerard Murphy (narrator on 13 recordings), Ian Holm (performer on 13 recordings), Jane Morgan (director on 13 recordings), Michael Bakewell (radio adaptor on 13 recordings), Penny Leicester (director on 13 recordings), and Stephen Oliver (composer on 13 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include epic fantasy, quest and fellowship, the One Ring and burden of power, Middle-earth, war against Sauron, and BBC prestige literary adaptation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Original 26-part BBC Radio 4 serial, Thirteen-part hour-long re-edit, Earlier BBC Lord of the Rings adaptation, and 2002 BBC reissue and rerun.
